This does not appear to be correct, because the first Websocket frame sent on the *connection* is being treated as the "first frame" for all Websocket *messages*. It doesn't work for Websocket connections with multiple messages (particularly if some are compressed and some not.)

commits_data.title: Websocket: Fix potential crash on invalid proto data key lookup
commits_data.message:
Websocket: Fix potential crash on invalid proto data key lookup

Websocket proto data is used for storing two types data, one where
the key is known in advance and one where key is based on packet
offsets. Update the known key to a very unlikely number to avoid
key clash which potentially could lead to dereferencing an invalid
pointer.

commits_data.title: Websocket: Fix decompression on fragmented packets
commits_data.message:
Websocket: Fix decompression on fragmented packets

The Per-Message Compressed (PMC) bit indicating whether a message is
compressed is per specification only set on first fragment. Keep
PMC info from first fragment and use when deciding whether to
decompress subsequent continuation frames.

While at it refactor the handling of opcode from first fragment to
make use of a common first_frag indication.

commits_data.title: Websocket: Fix follow websocket stream on compressed data
commits_data.message:
Websocket: Fix follow websocket stream on compressed data

Follow websocket stream currently taps unmasked payload data. The
data may as well be compressed. To allow cleartext data output also
when compression is enabled tap data after both unmasking and
decompression has happended.
